gen-dafont-bloody-archivo: Bloody swings in with big round lowercase bowls and a commanding growl. Archivo follows in sans, editorial but approachable, its curves opening outward so the heading's bluster has someone friendly to hand off to.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-fs-public-sans: Public Sans reads sturdy and trustworthy, a hefty lowercase with broad open counters that never crowd a line. Bushcraft sprawls above it in extra-wide, pen-drawn letters, expressive where the plain sans stays practical.
gen-dafont-stentiga-fs-asap: Spread-out, refined, and a touch luxurious. Asap, a plain sans, takes over where Stentiga's widely tracked letters leave off: the heading is made for looking at, the body for reading, with open arcs and tall lowercase.
gen-dafont-capture-smallz-fs-epilogue: Capture Smallz stamps down big-bodied lowercase letters with a raw, tactical bluntness, and nothing about it is delicate. Epilogue, a plain sans, then keeps a long read friendly, its wire-like monoline strokes running smoothly with no swelling at the joins.
gen-dafont-college-fs-supreme: Dynamic and authoritative from the first glance. College fills its tall lowercase with big counters, while Supreme sets a crisp, heavy-looking band of sans-serif text beneath, keeping its letters held open.
gen-dafont-conthrax-fs-fira-sans: Geometric and clean, Conthrax stretches wide across the top with towering lowercase. Its job is the strong first impression, while Fira Sans handles the steady work of reading, with a large x-height and openly curved s shapes.
gen-dafont-disorder-manrope: Manrope reads bright and approachable, every curved letter leaving a generous gap at its mouth. Its strongest quality is how smoothly it tames Disorder, whose raw, widely spaced glyphs and big lowercase would otherwise run wild.
gen-dafont-dogica-general-sans: Heavy and commanding, Dogica runs its wide tracking across the line with lowercase rising near the capitals. And General Sans, a sans-serif with a generous x-height, gives that weight its best quality: a smooth, professional readability.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-switzer: A towering lowercase gives Eight Bit Dragon its adventurous stride, spaced wide and relaxed across the line. And Switzer's wire-like, tubular letterforms supply the pair's best quality, a Swiss tidiness that never fights that swagger.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-fs-supreme: Ethnocentric pushes its big-bowled letters apart with fast, aggressive energy, short ascenders and all. Supreme does the quieter job, laying a crisp, heavy strip of sans text that stays open.
